quest.title: Target: Master of the Snowy Peaks!
quest.description: Farabi has sent a message asking you to meet him at Dragonspine. The target for today seems to be the legendary king of Snowboars...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventurer's Experience x2, Wanderer's Advice x4

dialogues.speaker: Edmund
dialogues.text: You're here, Traveler. Phew... That's a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's Edmund and Farabi. Why did you suddenly come to Dragonspine? Paimon was pretty surprised that you'd ask to meet here.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: Haha, this is quite sudden, but since an "unexpected research target" has appeared, I can't let go of this opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: Yes. Mr. Edmund says that he's seen huge animal footprints at the foot of the snowy mountain, and we finally found similar prints around this area.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: I can thus confirm that a huge Snowboar does indeed live there!

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: If we can get samples of its hair and blood, they will be a huge help in figuring out Snowboars' living conditions, and why they appeared at the foot of the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So our objective today is to hunt down that huge Snowboar?

dialogues.speaker: Edmund
dialogues.text: No, it's not a hunt. In the legends we hunters tell, the huge Snowboar is the true master of Dragonspine, and it is not something you can just hunt.

dialogues.speaker: Edmund
dialogues.text: But I suppose it'll be alright if we trap it for a short while for research purposes, right? You gotta help me out on this, Farabi.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: Mm, don't you worry. Honestly, after learning that Mondstadt is always plagued by Forest Boars during harvest season, I've been thinking a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: If all goes well, I'll continue my research on Forest Boars and maybe even find a solution to the problem.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: After all, one of the most important purposes of studying creatures is to find a way to live in harmony with them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, looks like you've learned a lot from your Weinlesefest vacation.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: Yeah. I had great wine, made friends, and found a goal to work towards. But let's hold the sentimental stuff off for after we get down from this mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Edmund
dialogues.text: Traveler, judging by the size of those prints, I strongly doubt I'll be a match for that Snowboar. So I'm gonna have to leave it to an expert like you, if that's alright.

dialogues.speaker: Edmund
dialogues.text: But please rest assured that I've set up the bait and some traps. Those should be of some help.

dialogues.speaker: Farabi
dialogues.text: Traveler, if you're ready, I'm going to ignite the bait and lure the Snowboar over.

choices.text: Hold on, I need more time to prepare.

response.speaker: Farabi
response.text: It's okay, take your time. We're dealing with a chunky fellow, after all.
